ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $CD$ is the altitude to the hypotenuse $AB$, and $\angle ACD=40^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle B$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: \textbf{Solution:} Given that in the right-angled triangle $ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $\angle ACD=40^\circ$, it follows that $\angle DCB=50^\circ$. Since $CD$ is the altitude from the hypotenuse $AB$, we have $\angle CDB=90^\circ$. In the right-angled triangle $CDB$: $\angle B=180^\circ-\angle DCB-\angle CDB=180^\circ-50^\circ-90^\circ=\boxed{40^\circ}$.
